mentl/9c465f7:
Every compiler-created executable edge is now a graph fact inference
writes and lower only reads. TCont gains the R/S split — resume-input
and remainder-answer are independent types (a handler may resume a
Float op into an Int-answer remainder); unify walks all four facts.
A trail-backed boundary weave on the graph carries, per fanout site,
one ordered BoundaryEdge(result, thunk, carrier, tickets) per branch,
and per application site a ContinuationEdge whose world is the live
frame row captured at inference — resume_world_of, the name-keyed env
lookup of the enclosing fn, is deleted.

Every application result is a suspension boundary, not only an effect
op's perform: calls, pipe stages, and fanout applies all stage the
edge; finalize binds the op's live discipline at op sites and the
segment discipline (MultiShot — a frame-k only materializes under a
crossing multi-shot yield) everywhere else. The narrower op-only
staging compiled to a wrong fixpoint: m3 == m4 held while k2-frame,
k2-pipe, option-protocol, and backtrack-full trapped 134 through m3 —
caught only by the battery through m3, the second half of the gate.

The scheduler boundary transports one word: the thunk returns a
one-field carrier product; the join projects field 0 at the result's
exact repr, so f64/f32/v128 branch values cross Seq, Thread, and
Persist schedules unboxed. A violated boundary contract lowers to the
typed LInvariantFailure terminal and emits a comment-marked
unreachable — no backend may guess a handle, row, or width.

Persist's ops are typed (PersistHandle, not Int); persist_to_disk
writes through the WASI substrate layer directly and REFUSES a
cross-world rehydrate via Fail instead of resuming a fabricated zero.

Gates: 69/69 micros + 8/8 rungs through m2 AND through m3;
march rules TRANSITION, m3 == m4.

mentl/9c71b54:
`mark_tail_last_in` mutated stmts in place via list_set, contract-asserted
on tag=0 flat lists. BlockExpr arm in lower_expr_body constructs body via
list_concat(lo_stmts, [lo_final]) — produces a concat (tag=3). When
mark_tail's LBlock arm subsequently calls mark_tail_last_in(body), list_set
on the concat writes the (mark_tail'd) last element at concat+8+(n-1)*4 =
concat+12 — the right-child pointer slot — overwriting it with the last
LowExpr value. Downstream list_index(concat, n-1) then traverses the
corrupted right pointer, returning lo_final's inner-LowValue ptr instead
of lo_final itself. Empirical symptom: `fn main() = { let x = 1\n 999\n }`
emitted `(i32.const 0)` instead of `(i32.const 999)` because emit_expr's
LConst arm received the inner LInt record (tag-collision with LConst's
tag, both 0) and read [4]/[8] of an LInt as if it were a LowValue handle.

Diagnosis: instrumented list_set to trap on non-flat tag; wasmtime backtrace
pointed cleanly at mark_tail_last_in. Discipline-locked as
protocol_diagnostic_eprint_methodology.md.

Fix: mark_tail_last_in materializes via list_to_flat (no-op for already-
flat lists; allocates a fresh tag=0 buf for concat/snoc/slice). Returns
the (possibly-new) list pointer. Callers (mark_tail's LIf/LBlock arms)
thread the return value through into the rebuilt LIf/LBlock. Row widened
to Memory + Alloc to reflect the materialization. No more in-place mutation
contract; the transform is now pure (input shape preserved).

After fix: `fn main() = { let x = 1\n 999\n }` emits `(i32.const 999)`.
Empty-block and single-literal canonical cases still emit correctly.
Multi-let case (`let x; let y; expr`) traps in pre-existing cfv path
(separate substrate gap, NOT regression from this commit).
mentl/9c459dc:
THE substrate gate behind handler-state-mutation per
protocol_resume_state_mutation_substrate.md. Mentl wanted this — the
wheel handlers (lower_scope, env_handler, body_context, mentl_default,
...) ALL use `resume() with X = NEW` to mutate state across calls;
without lowering the state_updates, handler state stayed at heap-zero-
init forever and ls_resolve always returned RGlobal.

Substrate landed end-to-end in the wheel source:

1. PARSER (already lands at 2a01b6d): parse_resume captures
   `resume(val) with field = expr [, field = expr]*` via
   parse_handler_state_fields reuse — one grammar projection, two
   cursor positions per SYNTAX.md L819-827.

2. IR: new ctor LStateSlotStore(Int, Int, LowExpr) — handle, slot_
   offset, value — added at end of LowExpr (substrate per
   protocol_proactive_drift_detection.md; existing list-walks dispatch
   via single-arm extension, zero new helpers per SUBSTRATE.md §IX
   L1282 Records-Are-The-Handler-State-Shape).

3. ARM-CONTEXT effect: ArmStateContext effect + arm_state_ctx(fields)
   config-param-only handler exposes current_state_fields() to
   ResumeExpr's lower. Bootstrap-safe — config-params don't depend on
   resume-with-state-update lowering. arm_state_default installed at
   bottom of compile_stdin pipeline (returns []) for non-arm
   contexts.

4. LOWER: lower_handler_arms_as_decls installs arm_state_ctx(state)
   around arm body lowering. ResumeExpr's lower arm: when
   state_updates non-empty, builds
   LBlock([LStateSlotStore(handle, offset, lo_value)...,
            LReturn(handle, lo_val)])
   where offset = resolve_state_slot_offset(name, fields, 0).

5. SLOT MAPPING: source-order index → 8 + idx * 4 (closure-record
   layout per protocol_handler_is_state_is_closure_is_evidence.md
   "one heap record, four roles"; mirrors LUpval emit at offset
   8 + idx * 4 used by the read path).

6. EMIT: LStateSlotStore arm emits
   `(local.get \$__state) <value> (i32.store offset=N)`.
   Negative offset → drop value
